extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and those tracking wartime European military/diplomatic developments (May 1940)
extracted.subtask_description: A contemporary news dispatch reporting military operations, diplomatic actions, consular advisories, and civil-defense measures across multiple European countries during early World War II. Includes field-censor notices and official State Department text.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Department duty to warn and assist citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: “The duty of the government towards its citizens in a war area is accomplished when it has advised them of the dangers of the situation and invited them to leave, while affording those who chose to go every possible assistance in obtaining transportation, and those who chose to remain, such protection as may be possible.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dispatch prints the Department's policy text and explains its practical application: officers abroad are invited to warn Americans, advise evacuation to the Bordeaux region (or Spain/Portugal), and the department will consider arranging evacuation by American vessels from those areas. Emphasizes discretionary authority of officers to invite Americans to leave and provide assistance but not to compel departure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consular evacuation advice and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Consuls in affected regions are advising Americans to concentrate at Bordeaux, France (or proceed to Spain or Portugal) instead of Genoa, and officials "will then consider the making of arrangements for their evacuation by American vessels from those areas."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance for evacuees: destination concentration points (Bordeaux/Spain/Portugal), and a promise that the State Department may arrange ship evacuation from those ports. The article notes complications (neutrality law restrictions) and shipping realities that affect implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutrality Act constraints on shipping and port access
rubrics_metrics.description: “American ships are not allowed to enter Bordeaux under the neutrality act, Nor are Americans allowed to sail on belligerent ships.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports the legal constraint that complicates evacuation: neutrality law prevents American vessels from entering certain belligerent ports and bars Americans from sailing on belligerent-flag ships, meaning Presidential action or other arrangements would be required to allow evacuation via Bordeaux.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field censorship of frontline dispatches
rubrics_metrics.description: Dispatches and reports are often marked "(Passed by Field Censor)" or described as censored; some battlefield details are omitted or labeled "censored."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that wartime reports are subject to military/civil censorship; reporters note when pieces have passed censorship. This affects the level of detail published and signals to readers that sensitive information may have been redacted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of qualified attribution for uncertain wartime information
rubrics_metrics.description: The article repeatedly uses source-qualifying phrases such as "reported," "informed spokesmen estimate," "foreign observers estimate," "was reported to have burned," and similar attributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects a journalistic practice in wartime reporting: qualify uncertain or second-hand information, attribute to named or anonymous sources, and avoid presenting unverified estimates as absolute fact. Many statements are presented as "reported" or "estimated" to signal uncertainty or lack of direct confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutrality/avoidance-of-provocation standard for neutral states
rubrics_metrics.description: “Throughout all these preparations the Swiss paid particular care to avoid any action which might be construed as unneutral.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the policy standard for neutral countries: take defensive precautions (mining bridges, guarding radio/telegraph/telephone centers, massing troops at borders) while avoiding acts that could be interpreted as taking sides. Operational measures must be balanced against maintaining neutral status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment of maritime contraband-control stations to changing belligerent status
rubrics_metrics.description: An economic-warfare official announced that the spread of the war to the Low Countries had removed the need for contraband control bases in the British Isles and that three stations were being closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative criterion for naval/maritime control: when territories change to belligerent status, contraband-control bases and their staffing are adjusted (closures or skeleton staffing) to reflect new operational priorities; maintain minimal capability for remaining relevant routes (e.g., examine ships bound for neutral Sweden).
